rows.grounds: compound of khaṇḍa and ātmā in nominative singular masculine

items.question: How does the part-self pervade the world when it is devoid of the universal self?
premises: The universal self pervades all things.
The part-self pervades the world when devoid.
Knowledge of self and other arises mutually.
items.inference: Thus world-pervasion by part-self depends on absence of universal self.
uncertainties: The exact referent of varjite is not specified.
The scope of etat remains context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Just as this is pervaded by that, so the world is pervaded by the part-self when devoid.
